name: Self-Strengthening Movement
title: The story of the Self-Strengthening Movement

text: More than 160 years ago, China, ruled by the Qing emperors, had lost wars against Britain and France.
At the same time, great rebellions were tearing the empire apart.
src: ruled from Beijing by the Manchu Qing dynasty / After defeat in the Second Opium War / In the Second Opium War (1856–1860) British and French forces took the Dagu forts / years: 1861 to 1895
At the same time the empire was torn by rebellion

text: Qing officials decided to “strengthen themselves” by using Western weapons, ships and machines.
But they meant to keep the old Confucian order, and the exams for officials stayed as they were.
src: Qing officials set out to “strengthen themselves” by adopting Western arms, ships and industry / learning the foreigners’ techniques in arms, ships and machines
while keeping the Confucian order / the examination system, which shaped the education and careers of officials, stayed as it was

text: They built arsenals, factories that made weapons, and shipyards, like the Jiangnan Arsenal in Shanghai.
They also opened schools and put Western books on science into Chinese.
src: Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang found the Jiangnan Arsenal at Shanghai / arsenals that made rifles, artillery and ammunition, shipyards that built steamships
the Jiangnan Arsenal’s translation department put Western works on science and engineering into Chinese / schools of languages, science and military and naval training

text: Li Hongzhang led the movement for a quarter of a century, starting companies, coal mines, a telegraph service and a navy.
Young Chinese students were sent to study in America, Britain and France.
src: Li Hongzhang, his protégé, dominated the movement for a quarter of a century from Tianjin, founding arsenals, enterprises, schools and the Beiyang Fleet / the Kaiping coal mines in 1877 and the Imperial Telegraph Administration in 1881
the first Educational Mission students sail for America / graduates of the Fuzhou school went on to study in Britain and France

text: But the government itself was not reformed, and the projects stayed scattered and short of money.
About 130 years ago, Japan, which had reformed its government, army and schools together, defeated China in a war.
src: Without reform of government, finance or education its gains stayed scattered / The central government lacked the revenue and authority
Japan, which since the Meiji Restoration of 1868 had reformed its government, army, schools and economy together, defeated the Qing on land and sea

text: After this defeat, reformers demanded bigger changes to the way China was governed.
Some of its work lasted: the Jiangnan Arsenal became a great shipyard, and the China Merchants' company still exists.
src: The defeat discredited the policy of borrowing techniques alone and led reformers to demand changes in institutions
The Jiangnan Arsenal grew into one of China’s great shipyards, and the China Merchants’ company survives as a business group today
